items.statement: Final: addition, ring expansion and ring closure explain the target skeleton
items.expected: Finally, use bond-forming/bond-breaking events and electronic-state changes supported by actual calculations to explain conversion of the given substrate to the given cyclopropane-fused [5.1.0] product through a bounded photosensitized open-shell addition–ring-expansion–ring-closure pathway. Integrate the intermediate local results with the correct target connectivity and DMSO/TXO irradiation conditions. Merely listing intermediates or restating the product does not earn credit. Equivalent nomenclature and equivalent physical explanations supported by actual evidence are acceptable; an arbitrary different mechanism is not automatically equivalent to the paper's result. Proof of a unique mechanism, ISC rates, all competing channels or the 99% yield is not required.

items.statement: Final: the cis preference explains the observed relative stereochemistry
items.expected: Finally, explicitly connect the calculated preference for cis over trans in this system to the observed same-face relationship of the C1 methoxycarbonyl/C7 phenyl groups, providing a bounded energetic/structural explanation. Distinguish the thermodynamic product preference from possible selectivity factors involving ring closure/crossing. Merely stating that cis is more stable without applying the evidence to the given stereochemical result is insufficient. The lower cis crossing point may be incorporated but need not be the sole cause. Without a valid rate/kinetic model, do not directly equate the energy difference with precise selectivity or a room-temperature isomerization rate, or treat the 99% isolated yield as dr. Thermal experiments on other products 22/27 are not direct kinetic evidence for this product.
